voices.excerpt: **Proposed Answer** The definitive, independent public source for a complete timeline of Italian government durations is the **Italian Ministry of the Interior’s “Historical Archive of Governments” (Archivio Storico dei Governi)**, which is published on the Ministry’s official website (https://www.interno.gov.it/it/ministero/archivio-storico-dei-governi). This archive is compiled from the official parliamentary records (the *Gazzetta Ufficiale* and the Senate/Chamber of Deputies’ legislative histories) and is regularly updated by the national statistical office (ISTAT) for statistical reporting. It lists every cabinet’s start and end dates, the prime minister, and the composition of the Council of Ministers, making it suitable for pinpointing the exact day when Giorgia Meloni’s cabinet exceeded the length of the previous longest post‑war government. **Why this source fits the question** | Observation | Inference | Uncertainty | |-------------|-----------|-------------| | The Ministry of the Interior maintains an official historical archive of all Italian governments. | The archive is an independent, government‑verified record, not a secondary news compilation. | Minor: occasional lag in updating the most recent cabinet dates (typically a few days). | | The archive’s data are cross‑referenced with the *Gazzetta Ufficiale* (the official journal of the Italian Republic). | The dates are legally binding and can be used as a definitive timeline. | None significant; the source is authoritative. | | ISTAT publishes statistical bulletins that cite the same dates for longitudinal analyses. | The timeline is also reflected in reputable international databases (e.g., Eurostat) that source from ISTAT. | None; consistency across sources reinforces reliability. | **Concrete Test to Verify the Answer** 1. **Locate the archive** – Visit the URL `https://www.interno.gov.it/it/ministero/archivio-storico-dei-governi` (or the English version if available). 2. **Identify the entry for “Giorgia Meloni II Cabinet”** – Note the “Date of formation” and the “Date of dissolution” (if any). 3. **Extract the duration** – Compute the number of days from formation to the current date (or to dissolution). 4. **Compare with the previous longest post‑war government** – The archive also lists the duration of the “Silvio Berlusconi IV Cabinet” (or any other historically longest cabinet). Verify that the Meloni cabinet’s day count has now exceeded that figure. 5. **Document the exact crossover date** – The archive’s chronological list will show the day on which the cumulative day count of the Meloni cabinet first surpassed the previous record; record that date as the definitive answer. If the archive shows the Meloni cabinet’s start date (e.g., 22 October 2022) and the calculated day count exceeds the prior record on, say, **15 May 2025**, then the archive provides the definitive timeline required. This test directly confirms that the proposed source contains the necessary, authoritative data.
